pagerbot: INCIDENT: INC-2026-045 - multiple 504s observed from ingress gateway (us-west-2) · Severity: P1 · paging oncall@sara

pagerbot: Alerts started at 2026-06-12T17:07:14Z — spike in 504/timeouts from /v1/generate across several upstream pools. Initial error rate ~18% on gateway pods.

sara (oncall): taking this. jumping in. who pushed anything to gateway in last 30m?

miguel (eng-sre): not me. I see a config rollout from li ~15m ago to add a new rate-limit policy, could be related.

li (prod-svc): yep pushed a rate-limit tweak for a customer burst test at 16:55. it was targeted, but may have mis-scoped route match. rolling back now.

anya (product): curious about customer impact — any reports yet?

miguel (eng-sre): looking at LB -> envoy logs, most 504s are gateway timing out to downstreams. problem: traces/req-id not propagating for ~40% of requests, so correlating is hard. logs are sparse.

ops-bot: deploy rollback started for deploy/gateway-config v2026.06.12-rc5 -> rolling back to v2026.06.11 (3/5 pods updated)

sara (oncall): ok prioritize visibility first. we need temporary instrumentation to unmask requests — add debug headers and full upstream response codes to logs. can someone patch a sidecar or envoy access log format quickly?

miguel (eng-sre): on it. quick plan: add an extra access_log with structured fields: request_id (if any), x-trace-id, upstream_status, upstream_time_ms, request_headers. will deploy as a non-blocking extra log sink to stdout.

li (prod-svc): rollback completed (all pods back to v2026.06.11). error rate dipped from 18% -> 11% in last 2m but still elevated.

sara (oncall): thanks. still needs live probe to tie 504 to a specific upstream. miguel, do we have a one-line filter to inject when header missing?

miguel (eng-sre): yes — using an Envoy header mutator filter that will insert a synthetic request_id when missing and emit a short debug marker. deploying as config patch to the gateway configmap. snippet: 

```yaml
# envoy header_mutation (temp)
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(handle)
        local id = handle:headers():get("x-request-id")
        if not id then
          handle:headers():add("x-request-id", "shim-" .. tostring(math.random(1000000)))
          handle:logInfo("shim-request-id-inserted")
        end
      end
```

miguel (eng-sre): patch applied to gateway-configmap -> kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway  (rolling restart in progress).

li (prod-svc): launching a synthetic probe across regions to exercise route and surface upstream latencies. also opening short-lived debug endpoint on the ingress pod to dump recent 504 traces: `kubectl exec -it gateway-0 -- cat /var/log/gateway/debug-last-200.log`

sara (oncall): good. also add a temporary log forwarder rule to push these debug logs to #incidents-logs-scratch so we can tail without digging into nodes. miguel can you do that?

miguel (eng-sre): pushed a fluent-bit rule that tags logs with tag=ingress-debug and filters for shim-request-id-inserted and upstream_status. forwarding now.

ops-bot: rollout status: deployment/gateway 2/5 updated, 3/5 pending. no crashloops.

anya (product): observed customer impact: two customers reported slow requests in our support queue, no major data loss but UX degraded. marking customer-impact true.

li (prod-svc): dug into a gateway pod log snippet — many lines show upstream 504 but no x-request-id or traceparent header. upstream timeouts show ~30s time_to_first_byte then 504. looks like a backend connection exhaustion under the new rate-limit rule.

sara (oncall): ok mitigation path: 1) keep rollback 2) keep shim to generate ids 3) throttle/disable rate-limit policy until we can patch backend pools 4) create temporary routing rule to shift traffic off pool-b where errors concentrated. miguel, can you add a diversion rule?

miguel (eng-sre): adding a weighted route tweak to reduce pool-b traffic to 10% and send remainder to pool-a. applying now.

miguel (eng-sre): route patch applied. monitoring.

(2m later)

miguel (eng-sre): metrics: error rate back to 3.2% (from 18%), p95 latency improved. synthetic probes show successful upstream responses for requests now carrying shim request-ids.

li (prod-svc): confirmed specific customer replay: requests that previously timed out are returning 200 after diversion.

sara (oncall): nice work. we still have an observability gap: traces weren't propagated by client -> need an SDK/ingress check in our SDK docs + add a persistent requirement for x-request-id in gateway. create follow-ups:

- MIG-457: CI test to validate header propagation across gateway (miguel)
- PROD-812: Permanent access_log + distributed-tracing header enforcement (li)
- ENG-OPS-389: postmortem + customer comms draft (anya)

anya (product): I'll draft the customer note and flag impacted accounts to account management.

sara (oncall): final status: mitigation complete, traffic normalizing. keeping the shim for 2h then revert once we have ticketed follow-ups. if error rate creeps >5% we reopen page.

miguel (eng-sre): leaving extra logs forwarded for 90m, will remove fluent-bit rule after revert.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-045 status -> Mitigated (monitoring) · participants: sara, miguel, li, anya.

sara (oncall): thanks team. postmortem owner assigned to anya. tagging this thread for the postmortem assets. :white_check_mark:
